paper.title: Active Ranking from Pairwise Comparisons and when Parametric Assumptions Don't Help

settings.name_in_paper: Active ranking from pairwise comparisons (Borda scores, arbitrary comparison matrix)
unmapped: Goal: partition the n items into L sets of pre-specified sizes k_1<...<k_L by Borda score (includes top-k and full ranking); the learner knows the set sizes
Scores must be distinct at set boundaries (unique ranking)
settings.definition_quote: At each time instant, the algorithm can compare two arbitrary items ... the algorithm receives an independent draw of a binary random variable with success probability M_ij ... we say that a ranking algorithm A is δ-accurate for a comparison matrix M if ... P[S_hat_l = S_l for all l] >= 1-δ.

settings.name_in_paper: Active ranking from pairwise comparisons, stochastic regime (lower bound)
unmapped: Goal: partition items into sets of pre-specified sizes by Borda score
Pairwise probabilities bounded away from 0 and 1 (M_ij >= M_min)

settings.name_in_paper: Active ranking under parametric models (BTL/Thurstone-type), stochastic regime (lower bound)
unmapped: The learner knows the link CDF Phi of the parametric model M_ij = Phi(w_i - w_j)
Goal: partition items into sets of pre-specified sizes by score
Pairwise probabilities bounded below by M_min
settings.definition_quote: C_PAR(Phi) = {M_ij = Phi(w_i - w_j) for all i,j in [n], for some w in R^n}. ... we prove a lower bound that applies even to algorithms that are given a priori knowledge of the function Phi.

bound.expression_latex: \constup \log(\frac{n}{\delta}) \{ \sum_{i\in S_1} f_{AR}(\underline\Delta_{1,i}) + \sum_{l=2}^{L-1}\sum_{i\in S_l} \max\{f_{AR}(\underline\Delta_{l,i}), f_{AR}(\bar\Delta_{l,i})\} + \sum_{i\in S_L} f_{AR}(\bar\Delta_{L,i})\}

symbols.H_AR: sum over items of f_AR evaluated at the relevant score gaps (max of upper/lower gap for middle sets), f_AR(x)=log(2 log(2/x))/x^2

conditions: M in C(0): distinct scores at set boundaries

source.label: ThmRanking
source.quote: For any $\Pmat \in \comparisonclass[0]$, and any $\delta \in (0,0.14]$ the AR algorithm is $\delta$-accurate for $\Pmat$ using a query size upper bounded by $\constup \log( \frac{\numitems}{\delta}) \{ \sum_{i \in \S_1} \FAR( \gaplo{1}{i}) + ...\}$

results.notes: Gaps are Borda-score gaps to set boundaries. The bound holds on the event of probability >= 1-delta on which AR is correct; recorded as high probability.

bound.expression_latex: \clow \log(\frac{1}{2\delta}) \{ \sum_{i\in S_1} f_0(\underline\Delta_{1,i}) + \sum_{l=2}^{L-1}\sum_{i\in S_l}\max\{f_0(\underline\Delta_{l,i}), f_0(\bar\Delta_{l,i})\} + \sum_{i\in S_L} f_0(\bar\Delta_{L,i})\}

symbols.F_tau: complexity F(tau(M)): sum over items of 1/gap^2 to the relevant set boundaries (max over upper/lower for middle sets)

conditions: algorithm is uniformly delta-accurate over C(1/8)

source.label: ThmRanking
source.quote: For any $\delta \in (0, 0.14]$, consider a ranking algorithm that is uniformly $\delta$-accurate over $\comparisonclass[1/8]$. Then when applied to a given pairwise comparison model $\Pmat \in \comparisonclass[3/8]$, it must make at least $\clow \log(\frac{1}{2 \delta}) \{...\}$ comparisons on average.

results.notes: Proof gives c_low = 1/16. Change-of-measure lower bound.

symbols.F_tau: complexity F(tau(M)) = sum over items of 1/gap^2 to relevant set boundaries
symbols.M_min: lower bound on pairwise comparison probabilities
symbols.phi_min: lower bound on Phi' on [Phi^{-1}(M_min), Phi^{-1}(1-M_min)]
symbols.phi_max: upper bound on Phi' on that interval

conditions: algorithm is uniformly delta-accurate over C_PAR(Phi) ∩ C(M_min)
applied to M in C_PAR(Phi) ∩ C(M_min)
Phi continuous, strictly increasing, (phi_min, phi_max, M_min)-bounded derivative

source.label: thm:necessityparametric
source.quote: Given a tolerance $\delta \in (0, 0.15]$, and a continuous and strictly increasing CDF $\Phi$ whose derivative is $(\pdfmin,\pdfmax,\pmatmin)$-bounded, consider any algorithm that is uniformly $\delta$-accurate over $\parfamily \cap \comparisonclass[\pmatmin]$. Then, when applied to a given pairwise comparison matrix $\Pmat \in \parfamily \cap \comparisonclass[\pmatmin]$, it must make at least $\clobo \log (\frac{1}{2\delta}) \complexityP(\vscore(\Pmat))$ ... comparisons on average.

results.notes: Part (b) (realizability of any score vector by a parametric model) is a structural statement, not recorded as a bound.
